_doc: Per-reference load/pass-through current table for tools/fix/power_copper_audit_v2.py (classification of heavy loads on the power nets).
Values are DESIGN ASSUMPTIONS taken from the part roles on the board (tools/power_widths.json budgets, IS-1 10.1 eFuse limits,
datasheet-class ratings: TPS26630 eFuse, TPS26624 eFuse, TPS274C65 quad high-side switch, TPS1H000 high-side switch, TPS22990/TPS22918/
TPS2553 load switches, LM70660 / LMR36506 / TPS6290x bucks, TPS7A16/TPS7A26 LDOs, TMR 4WI isolated converters, MAX17612 current limiters).
They are NOT measurements. Order of precedence in the tool: refs[ref].nets[net] > refs[ref].amps > value_patterns (first match on the
footprint value) > pin-type default. Pins whose netlist pinfunction (suffix _<pin> removed) matches not_heavy_pinfunctions are bias/sense
pins (0.01 A) whatever the part. A part's amps are split evenly over its pads on that net (parallel VIN pins). A load is 'heavy' when the
PART's total current on the net >= heavy_threshold_amps (audit v2.1+; v2.0 compared the per-pad share). Connector pads on a supply net
(J/TB prefix) default to connector_default_amps unless listed. r3 (10 Oct 2026): the bare '74' logic pattern also matched Wurth 7499111446;
logic is now matched by the family prefixes SN74 / 74LV / 74AHC / 74HC.
Motor drivers: the motherboard carries no motor driver IC (the twelve motor interfaces drive external drivers through the
mc_motor_buffers logic; checked in sch.net 11 Oct 2026); the motor-side supply loads are the MOTOR_5V_A/B and PWM load switches
